2026-12-19.title: Third Saturday of Annunciation
2026-12-19.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Chosen by the grace of God
The one who comes from above is above all
2026-12-19.verse: He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure.
theo: Paul tells how God “set me apart before I was born and called me through his grace” and “was pleased to reveal his Son to me.” His Gospel is not human invention but revelation. Like Jeremiah and John the Baptist, Paul was called from the womb.

John the Baptist testifies: “The one who comes from above is above all… He whom God has sent speaks the words of God.” As Christmas approaches, the Church contemplates the One who comes from above: not a teacher among teachers, but the Son into whose hands the Father has given all things.
outline: Ask: how did God reveal his Son to you?
Jesus comes from heaven and speaks God's words.
In Christ, God gives himself fully.
“The one who comes from above is above all.”
live: Thank God today for the grace of your baptism and vocation.
Set up the crib at home this weekend with the family.
2026-12-19.prayer: Father, you set us apart and called us by grace. Prepare our hearts to welcome your Son who comes from above and gives the Spirit without measure. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the One who comes from above comes down upon our altar. Whoever receives him with faith has eternal life.

quick: God calls us before we are born.
Jesus comes from above and speaks God's words.
God gives the Spirit without measure.
2026-12-19.action: Set up the crib at home with your family.
2026-12-19.question: Is Christ “above all” in my life?

family.explain: John the Baptist said Jesus is the greatest, because he comes from heaven. John was happy to be small so that Jesus could be big.
family.intention: We pray for people who do not yet know Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make Jesus bigger in our family this Christmas?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you come from above and are above all. As we gather, help us decrease so that you may increase in us. Amen.
share: God set Paul apart before he was born (Galatians 1:15). How do I experience God's call in my life?
John says the one from above is above all (John 3:31). Is Jesus truly first in my life?
Whom do I know who is far from Christ, and how can I pray for them?
pm.resp: He must increase; we must decrease.
interc: For the Church, that she may always point to Christ, like John the Baptist.
For those who persecute Christians, that like Saul they may be converted.
For those far from faith, that the Son may be revealed to them.
For our young people, that they may discover God's call before their birth.
For our families, that Jesus may be first in our homes.
pm.close: Lord God, you revealed your Son to Paul and made him an apostle. Reveal him to us and to all who seek, and give us the eternal life that comes from believing in him. Amen.

illus: A young engineer in Bengaluru who had mocked his Christian roommate for years was given a New Testament as a joke gift. He read John's Gospel in one night. Two years later he was baptised. He said: “I didn't find him. He found me.”

homily: Dear friends, St Paul tells the Galatians how he received the Gospel: not from a human source, nor was I taught it, but I received it through a revelation of Jesus Christ (Galatians 1:12). He had been a violent persecutor of the Church. Then God, who had set me apart before I was born and called me through his grace, was pleased to reveal his Son to me (Galatians 1:15–16).

Paul's story shows that no one is beyond God's reach. The man who dragged Christians to prison became the apostle of the nations. God's call came before Paul's merits, even before his birth, just as it came to Jeremiah, to John the Baptist and to Mary.

In the Gospel John the Baptist says of Jesus: the one who comes from above is above all; he whose origin is in heaven testifies to what he has seen and heard. The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in his hands. Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life (John 3:31–36).
These are the words of the forerunner, who said: he must increase, but I must decrease. John knows his place. All his greatness is in pointing to the one who comes from above.

Christmas is about this one who comes from above. He is not one religious teacher among many; he is the Son, in whose hands the Father has placed all things. Believing in him is not one opinion among others; it is eternal life.

As Christmas approaches, let us ask: who comes first in my life? My plans, my image, my family, my career; or the One who comes from above? Let us decrease, so that he may increase, and let us pray for those who, like Saul, are far from Christ today. Amen.
kids: Children, God knew you even before you were born, and He loves you very much. Thank Him for your life today!

intro: Theme: “The One who comes from above.”
Paul called from the womb; John's witness to the One from heaven.

sub: Jeremiah, John and Paul were called from the womb.
Each of us has a vocation from God.
q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you.
The one who comes from above is above all; the one who is of the earth belongs to the earth and speaks about earthly things. The one who comes from heaven is above all.
points.apply: Thank God for your vocation today.

points.h: He speaks the words of God
sub: The Spirit is given without measure.
q: Then afterward I will pour out my spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy.
He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure.
points.apply: Pray to the Holy Spirit before reading the Gospel.

sub: The Father has given all to the Son.
Believing in him is eternal life.
q: For a child has been born for us, a son given to us; authority rests upon his shoulders.
The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in his hands.
points.apply: Set up the crib at home this weekend.

concl: The One from above is coming.
Let him be above all in our lives.
